documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
63M here to set up care. Prior PCP retired. Brought a bag of bottles, which helped.

Heart: two heart attacks. First in 2014, cathed and stented then; that was also when he put the cigarettes down for good. Second this past August, kept a few days at a regional hospital and sent home on the same pills, no new stent per his account. No chest pain since. Follows with an outside cardiology group.
Diabetes since roughly 2003, on insulin for years. Glargine 24 units at night plus metformin 1000 twice a day. Checks sugars when he remembers, mostly 140s to 180s fasting. Feet have been numb and tingly for a while.
BP and cholesterol on lisinopril, metoprolol, atorvastatin 40.
COPD: uses albuterol a few times a month, mostly cold air or heavy yard work. No hospital stays for breathing.
Seizures: complex partial spells as a younger man, none in many years on valproic acid 500 twice daily. Drives. Prior PCP refilled it.

Social: retired construction foreman, on disability. Married, wife at home. Former smoker, about 40 pack-years, quit 2014. Alcohol: 2 to 3 drinks every night, mostly whiskey. No drugs.
Family: father had his first MI at 58. Mother has type 2 diabetes. Sister with high blood pressure.
Allergies: none known.

Exam: well-appearing heavyset man. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs with mildly prolonged expiration, no wheeze. Abdomen soft. No leg swelling. Feet: skin intact, monofilament reduced over both soles, pulses palpable.

A/P:
1. CAD s/p MI x2, stent 2014. Aspirin, metoprolol, atorvastatin 40, lisinopril. Keep cardiology.
2. T2DM with neuropathy, on insulin. A1c and kidney labs today. Foot care reviewed.
3. HTN, at goal today.
4. Hyperlipidemia: lipid panel today.
5. COPD: albuterol PRN. Will get spirometry on file, none in what he brought.
6. Seizure history: valproic acid, level and CBC/LFTs today.
7. Alcohol: AUDIT-C 6. Talked plainly about drinking with his heart and his seizure med. He's thinking about it, not ready to set a date.
8. Health maintenance: flu shot today. Hep C and HIV once. Requesting records from the old office for colonoscopy and the cath reports.

RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Stanley, your labs are back. A1c 8.1, a bit above where we want it. Kidney and liver numbers fine. LDL 68 is good on the atorvastatin. Triglycerides are high at 290; cutting back the evening drinks would help that more than anything. Seizure medicine level is right in range. Hep C and HIV negative. We'll go over it in January.

documents.title: Prior primary care records (summary)
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
86 pages faxed by the prior PCP office. Abstracted for the chart:
- 2014: MI at a regional hospital, cardiac cath with PCI and stent. Discharge summary and cath report included.
- 08/2018: second MI, regional hospital, managed medically. Discharge summary included; meds unchanged on discharge.
- Seizure disorder: complex partial seizures, on valproic acid long term, no events documented in the notes we have.
- Colonoscopy 2016: normal to the cecum, no polyps, 10-year recall.
- Diabetes: insulin glargine since about 2012 per the notes.
- Immunizations: Pneumovax listed years ago, no date.
Scanned to Media. PCP to review.

S: Masked visit. Cramping and weak legs, thighs and hips mostly, started roughly two weeks after he went up to atorvastatin 80 (changed 5/13). Hard getting up from a low chair and the cramps cut his walks short. No dark urine, no fever. Still on fenofibrate. He mentions the January cholesterol visit and that he had been feeling fine before the dose change.
Hx: CAD with MI two years ago and in 2014, stent. T2DM, HTN.

A/P: Statin-associated muscle symptoms, likely made worse by fenofibrate on top of the higher dose.
- Stop atorvastatin 80 and fenofibrate now.
- CK, liver panel, BMP today.
- Plan to retry atorvastatin 40, which he took for years without trouble, once he's back to normal.
Will call with results.

documents.title: Cardiology consultation
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology group
Date of visit: 12/14/2020
Reason: exertional chest tightness

Mr. Conti, 65, known CAD with MIs in 2014 and 2018 and a stent in 2014, and statin intolerance at high dose this summer, now back on atorvastatin 40. He describes a central squeezing tightness going uphill or up stairs that settles with rest.
Medications: aspirin 81, metoprolol succinate 50, atorvastatin 40, lisinopril 20, metformin 1000 BID, insulin glargine, valproic acid, albuterol PRN.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Social: former smoker. No alcohol.
Vitals stable. Exam: regular rhythm, no murmur, lungs clear, no edema.
Stress test today reproduced his usual tightness with ischemic ST changes, recovering promptly.

Impression: stable angina pectoris, chronic CAD. Medical management.
Plan:
1. Nitroglycerin 0.4 mg SL as needed. Sit down before using it, as it can make him lightheaded. Must never be combined with erectile dysfunction pills of the PDE-5 type. He tried a tablet in clinic after the test, with relief within a few minutes.
2. Continue aspirin, metoprolol, atorvastatin, lisinopril.
3. Follow-up in 3 months.

Cardiology

conditions.label: Type 2 diabetes mellitus with foot ulcer
conditions.note: right plantar first metatarsal head, 2 cm

documents.title: Podiatry consultation
documents.author: podiatry
documents.body:
Outside podiatry practice
Date of visit: 12/13/2021

Referred by his PCP for a right foot wound. 66-year-old man with type 2 diabetes for about 18 years, neuropathy, CAD with stable angina followed by cardiology. His wife noticed blood on his sock about three weeks ago; no pain. Years of night-time numbness and tingling in both feet; recently hard to feel the gas pedal. No fever, chills or drainage; walking unaffected. No back pain or radiating leg symptoms. No prior amputations. Admits he doesn't look at his feet regularly, hasn't seen podiatry in years, and wears one pair of worn work shoes daily. Quit smoking years ago.
ROS: no vision change, falls, bowel or bladder trouble, hand numbness, weight loss or fatigue.
Meds per patient: metformin, insulin glargine, lisinopril, atorvastatin, aspirin, metoprolol, valproic acid, albuterol.
Allergies: none known.

Exam: afebrile. Right plantar first metatarsal head: 2.0 cm shallow ulcer, clean granular base, hyperkeratotic rim. No erythema, edema or fluctuance. Probe to bone negative. Semmes-Weinstein: protective sensation absent over both plantar surfaces including toes and heels. Vibration decreased at both halluces. Capillary refill delayed. DP and PT diminished on the right.
Most recent A1c 8.9%.
ABI in office: right 0.62, left 1.02.

Assessment: neuropathic diabetic foot ulcer right plantar first MTP region, no clinical infection. Peripheral arterial disease right leg by ABI.
Plan: debrided callus; offloading felt and post-op shoe; daily dressing changes taught. Foot X-ray. Vascular surgery consult given the ABI. Back in 3-4 weeks.

Podiatry

reports.text: Right foot, three views. No fracture or dislocation. No cortical erosion or periosteal reaction at the first metatarsal head. No soft-tissue gas. Joint spaces preserved. Scattered vascular calcification.

documents.title: Foot X-ray copy

documents.title: Vascular surgery consultation
documents.author: vascular surgery
documents.body:
Outside vascular surgery group
Date of visit: 01/12/2022

Asked by podiatry to see Mr. Conti for a right plantar forefoot ulcer with a right ABI of 0.62 (left 1.02). He has no rest pain and no calf claudication he can name; the neuropathy may mask some of it. Former smoker. Diabetic on insulin. CAD with prior stent, on aspirin and atorvastatin.
Allergies: NKDA.
Exam: right foot warm, capillary refill sluggish, DP and PT diminished on the right, normal on the left. The ulcer is smaller than podiatry's measurement, clean, no infection.
Impression: peripheral arterial disease of the right leg; neuropathic ulcer that is already healing with offloading.
Plan: no intervention while the ulcer heals. Walking program, continue aspirin and statin, glucose control. Podiatry to keep offloading and wound care. If the ulcer stalls or he develops rest pain, we will see him back for imaging and discussion.

Vascular Surgery

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: hospitalist
documents.body:
Regional hospital, cardiac surgery service
Admitted 05/14/2024. Discharged 05/26/2024.

Principal diagnosis: acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction.
Procedures: emergent cardiac catheterization with reperfusion of the culprit lesion; coronary artery bypass grafting, multivessel (05/19/2024).

Course: 68-year-old man with CAD (MIs 2014 and 2018, stent 2014), HFrEF, type 2 diabetes, COPD and a seizure disorder, who woke with crushing chest pain and arrived by ambulance with ST elevation on ECG. Taken directly to the cath lab; the culprit was reperfused and catheterization showed multivessel disease. Heart team recommended surgical revascularization, performed on hospital day 6. Post-operative course without major complication; extubated on schedule, chest tubes removed, ambulating the halls before discharge. No seizures during the stay; valproic acid continued.

Allergies: NKDA.
Discharge medications: aspirin 81 daily, metoprolol succinate 50 daily, atorvastatin 40 daily, lisinopril 20 daily, furosemide 20 daily, metformin 1000 twice daily, insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime, valproic acid 500 twice daily, albuterol as needed, nitroglycerin SL as needed.
Follow-up: cardiothoracic surgery in 3 days; cardiology in 4-6 weeks; PCP within 1-2 weeks; outpatient cardiac rehabilitation referral placed.
Sternal precautions: no lifting over 10 lb, no driving for 4 weeks.

reports.text: PA and lateral. Median sternotomy wires intact and aligned. Small left pleural effusion with blunting of the left costophrenic angle. No pneumothorax. No focal consolidation. Cardiac silhouette enlarged, as before.

Regional hospital emergency department
Date of visit: 12/11/2025

CC: three days of right heel-cord pain, can't put weight on it.
HPI: 70M with CAD s/p CABG, HFrEF, insulin-treated T2DM with neuropathy, depression followed by psychiatry since his 2024 STEMI, and a prior right foot ulcer seen by podiatry. Three days ago, walking down a flight of stairs, felt a sudden sharp stabbing pain at the back of the right ankle, worse with any motion, with a clicking sensation near the heel. No fall or blow, no fever, no swelling elsewhere. Started ciprofloxacin 5 days ago at urgent care for a UTI; no steroid use.
He also says his mood has slid badly over the last month since his mother was told she has metastatic small cell lung cancer. Feels helpless and guilty, tired, sleeping through the day, skipping meals, has stopped going to the senior center. Admits he's been missing doses of his medicines. Denies suicidal ideation. His sister keeps pushing him to sign estate papers while their mother is still on chemo, and the calls leave him overwhelmed; he's been letting them go to voicemail. Had a video visit with his PCP yesterday for refills and didn't mention the ankle.
PMH: CAD with MIs 2014, 2018 and 05/2024 STEMI, CABG 2024, stent 2014; HFrEF; T2DM; HTN; HLD; COPD; complex partial seizures on valproic acid; MDD.
Meds: metoprolol, atorvastatin, lisinopril, aspirin, metformin, valproic acid, insulin glargine, albuterol PRN, ciprofloxacin.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: former smoker, 40 pack-years. Former heavy whiskey drinker, 2-3 a night, none since 2019.
Family: mother with metastatic small cell lung cancer.

Vitals: T 36.9 C, P 72, RR 14, BP 136/82.
Exam: looks older than his years, no distress. Antalgic gait, favoring the left. Right posterior ankle just above the heel: mild swelling and point tenderness; tendon thicker than the left. Thompson test: plantar flexion diminished with calf squeeze. Passive dorsiflexion sharply painful. Plantar flexion weak. No redness, warmth or crepitus. Sensation and pulses intact.
Labs: WBC, ESR and CRP normal.
X-ray right ankle: mild degenerative change, no fracture or calcification.

Impression: right Achilles tendinopathy with suspected rupture, likely from the fluoroquinolone.
Plan: stop ciprofloxacin; cephalexin 500 mg twice daily for 3 days to finish the UTI course. Walking boot with heel lift, crutches, no weight bearing until seen. Orthopedics referral, appointment within the week. Acetaminophen for pain, avoid NSAIDs with his heart failure. Avoid fluoroquinolones in future. Worsening depression: no SI, safe for discharge with his wife; encouraged to call his psychiatrist and PCP this week. Return for calf swelling, chest pain or thoughts of self-harm.

A/P:
1. Right Achilles tendinopathy, suspected rupture, after ciprofloxacin. Boot, crutches, ortho Friday. Ciprofloxacin added to the allergy list as an intolerance; no fluoroquinolones going forward.
2. MDD, worse with family stressors, PHQ-9 15, no SI. Sent a message to his psychiatrist today asking for an earlier visit; they'll call him. Safety plan reviewed. Weekly check-in calls from our RN until then.
3. Missed doses: pillbox set up with wife; he agreed to let her help with the evening ones.

Objective: right ankle swelling mild, tender mid-tendon; limited dorsiflexion, guarded; plantar flexion weak. Protective sensation absent both feet (known neuropathy), skin intact.
Plan: 2x weekly for 8-10 weeks. Wedge weaning per ortho protocol, gentle range of motion, progressive calf loading, balance work. Skin checks given neuropathy.

Physical Therapy

documents.title: update
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Down to one wedge in the boot. PT says I'm ahead of schedule. Feeling a bit better on the higher dose of the sertraline. My mother finished her second round of chemo. Do you need to see me before March?

documents.title: RE: update
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good to hear on all fronts. March is fine unless something changes. Keep your feet checked with the boot on and off, the skin under it can rub without you feeling it.

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Out of the boot as of last week, in sneakers with a heel lift. PT twice a week. Mood a good deal better on sertraline 100 and the therapy sessions; PHQ-9 9, down from 15. Back to the senior center Tuesdays. Mother still on treatment. Taking meds from the pillbox, wife does the evening fill.
No chest pain, no swelling, breathing usual.
Exam: walks with a slight limp. Right Achilles thickened, mildly tender, intact. Feet: skin intact, no pressure areas from the boot. Heart regular, lungs clear, no edema.
A/P: MDD improving. Achilles partial tear healing, PT. T2DM: A1c today, sugars were higher during the bad weeks. HFrEF, CAD stable. RTC July for AWV.

Right Achilles high-grade partial tear, nonoperative. Out of the boot about five weeks. Walking without a limp on level ground, mild ache after long walks. PT reports steady strength gains.
Allergies: ciprofloxacin.
Exam: tendon thickened, nontender, continuous. Thompson test normal plantar flexion. Single-leg heel raise not yet possible on the right.
Plan: finish PT, then home program. No return to ladders or jumping until he can do repeated single-leg heel raises. Follow up as needed.

documents.body:
AWV plus chronic care review.
Function: independent. Walking 30 minutes most days again, ankle good, finished PT in May. No falls. Driving.

Sober 7 years. Cognitive screen normal.
Heart: no angina, no nitro this year. No swelling or orthopnea. Cardiology in May, no changes.
Diabetes: pillbox routine holding, sugars back down per his meter.
Meds reviewed with bottles, list current. Ciprofloxacin intolerance on file.
Exam: regular, lungs with mild prolonged expiration, no edema. Right Achilles thickened, nontender. Feet: insensate soles, skin intact, right pulses faint.
Prevention: colonoscopy from 2016 is due; at 70 with his heart history he prefers a stool test, FIT kit given. LDCT ordered for the fall. Flu and COVID in the fall. Eye exam due August.
ACP: wife remains proxy; reviewed his wishes, unchanged.
Labs today. Follow-up booked for October.
